html:
José Eduardo dos Santos was president of Angola from 1979 to 2017, one of the longest-serving leaders in Africa.

A petroleum engineer trained in the Soviet Union, he took over the MPLA on the death of Agostinho Neto. He led the government through the civil war, turning from Marxism to the market, and after the war's end in 2002 presided over an oil boom and rebuilding with Chinese loans.

His family and allies grew very rich. His daughter Isabel was called Africa's richest woman, before investigations in 2020 into how she made her fortune. He stepped down in 2017, and his successor, João Lourenço, moved against his family. He died in Barcelona in 2022, having shaped modern Angola.
